This column stores the category ID of the financial class stored in a hospital billing transaction. For charges, the financial class comes from the hospital account that the charge is associated with. For payments, the financial class comes from the payer specified during payment posting. If no payer is specified during payment posting, the financial class is self-pay. If the adjustment is entered in adjustment posting, the financial class is from the payer specified in adjustment posting. Previously you could only access the first two lines with the columns PATIENTS.ADD_LINE_1 and PATIENTS.ADD_LINE_2. Now, there is a new table, called PAT_ADDRESS, which allows you to get all lines of the PATIENTS's permanent address. It is recommended to use this column to report on medication orders. If your search includes mixture components, make sure you also search ORDER_MEDMIXINFO.MEDICATION_ID in addition to this column.
The name of the medication.

"Indicates whether a medication order has been verified by the pharmacist as non-formulary. A ""Y"" indicates that the pharmacist verified the medication order as non-formulary. To find which orders were placed as non-formulary
"Indicates whether this order was placed as non-formulary prior to verification. A ""Y"" indicates a non-formulary medication."
If this order was an ADS override, this column indicates if it was a non-clinical override. Non-clinical overrides create charge only orders that do not show on the MAR.
Indicates whether the order is a one-step medication, a medication whose administration is documented in one step.

If your organization allows nurses to order medications on the fly, this will indicate if this is an on-the-fly medication order. An on-the-fly medication order is similar to an ADS override, except the order is created by scanning an NDC rather than pulling a drug from an ADS cabinet to create an interface message for a new order.

If a medication was ordered using an IMS orderable for Mixtures or Drips, this column will contain the medication ID of the Orderable record. This column should typically only be used for searching for use of specific Orderables.
The date of ORDERING_DTTM.
The unique, internal contact date of the ordering contact of the order. This column is frequently used to link to the ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO table.
The date and time the order was released. For other types of orders that are created on the fly like override pulls, one step medications, and bulk charges this is the time the order was created.
The hour of day of ORDERING_DTTM.
The unique ID of the provider who placed the medication order. This is commonly linked to the PROVIDERS table.
The discrete dose for a medication as entered by the user in the orders activity.
The end date and time of the order.
A link to the Order History activity for the EMR system-Crystal Integration. It displays as RX_ORDER_NM_WID.
The unique ID of the medication order.
The category name of the order priority.
The category number for the priority assigned to an order.
The ordered route of administration.
The start date and time of the order.

The unique ID of the PATIENTS department at the time the order was released. For override pulls and bulk charges, this is the dispense department of the order. If an order's department cannot be found, the department of the order's encounter is used instead (PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS.EFFECTIVE_DEPT_ID).
The name of the PATIENTS department at the time the order was released. For override pulls, this is the dispense department of the order.

The unique encounter identifier for the encounter the order was placed on. This number is unique across all PATIENTS encounters. If you use IntraConnect, this is the Unique Contact Identifier. This column is commonly used to join to the PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS table.
The unique ID of the PATIENTS record for this line. This column is frequently used to link to the PATIENTS table.
The unique ID of the revenue location of the PATIENTS department at the time the order was released or created.
The name of the revenue location of the PATIENTS department at the time the order was released or created.
This notes whether a frequency is designated as PRN (or as needed).
The name of the last queue reason. The possible values are in the description for RXQ_REASON_CODE.
The user who released the order.
The date the order was released. For conditional orders it is the initiation time. If the conditional order was never initiated, it is null. This column is commonly used as a date range in reports.

The category ID of the last reason the order went to the verify queue during the initial order verification process. This can include 1-New, 11-Override Pull, 15-First Verify, 16-2nd Verify, 17-Conditional, 18-Conditional 1rst, 19-Conditional 2nd, or 20-Conditional Initiate, 23-Review On-The-Fly, or 25-Deferred.
The order name from several possible sources in the following order of availability: display name, order description, and finally the name of the medication.
A unique order identifier that consists of RX_ORDER_NAME and the order ID. This column is often used for grouping, sorting and display purposes in reports.
The category ID of the last unqueue reason or action that was taken on the order by a user during the initial order verification process. This can include 1-Verified or 2-Rejected.
The name of the last unqueue action a user performed during the initial order verification process. The possible values are in the description for RX_UNQUEUE_REAS_CODE.
The date of VERIFY_QUEUE_ENTRY_DTTM.
The date and time the order entered the verify queue for the queue reason in QUEUE_REASON.
The hour of day of VERIFY_QUEUE_ENTRY_DTTM.
This item stores the login department of the verifying user, stored in the source item.
The user that took the action that caused the order to leave the verify queue.
The date of VERIFY_UNQUEUE_DTTM.
The date and time the user took action that caused the unqueue reason in UNQUEUE_REASON.
The hour of VERIFY_UNQUEUE_DTTM.
